decisions.reason: As a core bread that survived beyond launch and uses the bakery’s existing craft skills and inputs, it is inexpensive to keep and there is no clear negative signal strong enough to justify abandonment.
A sweet pastry fits the firm’s traditional confectionery range and can be continued at low option cost, so without evidence of weak demand management would likely leave it in the assortment.

This farmhouse bread is somewhat more exposed to rationalization because it overlaps with other breads, but it still sits close to the core business and is cheap enough to keep unless sales clearly disappoint.
The poppy seed Christmas stollen is a flagship-style product with a gold award and strong fit to the firm’s heritage seasonal specialties, so management would very likely continue it.
The premium Christmas stollen also has a gold award and suits the seasonal specialty business, though it faces some risk of pruning if management narrows the range around the flagship stollen.
